claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

1. **Do you have any children, and if so, how many?**

Please tell me about the children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 19 and still lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a son named Alex who is 19 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is over 16, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** 

(For example, this could include full-time non-advanced education like A-levels, Scottish Highers, or approved training courses.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Alex being in full-time education doing A-levels would typically mean you can continue to receive Child Benefit for him.

Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you the person responsible for Alex?** In other words, does he live with you, or if he lives elsewhere for his studies, are you contributing at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, accommodation costs, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he does live with me, but actually his other parent already claims Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. That's a key factor here.

Under the Child Benefit rules, **only one person can get Child Benefit for a child**. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be eligible to also claim for him.

If you wanted to claim Child Benefit for Alex instead, you would need to:
- Agree with the other parent that they would stop their claim
- Have them contact the Child Benefit Office to stop getting Child Benefit
- Then you would need to make a new claim yourself

But as things currently stand, with the other parent already claiming, you cannot also receive Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me provide you with my formal assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:** You are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time because his other parent is already claiming it. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child. If you and the other parent wanted to change who receives the benefit, you would need to agree on this together and follow the process I mentioned above.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
